title: Cycle-factors of regular graphs via entropy: the expected number of cycles of a random cycle-factor (Proposition 3.4)
author: Micha Christoph, Nemanja Dragani\'c, Ant\'onio Gir\~ao, Eoin Hurley, Lukas Michel, Alp M\"uyesser
work: Cycle-factors of regular graphs via entropy
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the proposition printed as Proposition 3.4 of "Cycle-factors of regular graphs via entropy" (source0.tex lines 246--251, source label prop:boundexpectednumberofcycles), delivered with the article's own complete proof at source0.tex lines 253--315 (63 lines, one adjacent proof environment). It bounds the expected number of cycles of an arbitrary random cycle-factor of a directed d-regular graph on n vertices by 2(n/d)(log d + 1) + (n/d) log_2(d!) - H(C), which is the technical core of the article and the input to its main theorems. The proof is complete inside the retained span: it represents the cycle-factor as a random permutation, applies the chain rule for entropy along a uniformly random vertex order, identifies the entropy loss compared with a uniform permutation, shows that the number of available out-neighbours is uniform on [d], converts the probability that a step closes a cycle into 2 over the number of available out-neighbours plus the entropy loss, and sums the resulting harmonic series. It is not a routine exercise: it is Radhakrishnan's proof of the Bregman-Minc inequality reworked with an explicit bookkeeping of the total entropy loss, and the article presents that bookkeeping as its new contribution. Required context: the article's own Lemma 3.3 on the probability of an atom of a random variable in terms of the entropy loss, retained in statement form. Rated H2 rather than H3 because the argument, although clever and research level, is a single entropy calculation built on a classical template that the article itself names.
